headline: Defining diversity and homology directly on pangenome graph structure
label: Pangenome Graph Diversity Measures
summary: Graph-based pangenome comparison is moving beyond sequence-level analysis toward quantities defined on graph structure itself.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is quantitative comparison of pangenome graphs as objects in their own right. One study interpolates and extrapolates node counts in colored compacted de Bruijn graphs, using Hill numbers to weight rare and common elements in a diversity measure defined over the graph. A second introduces a homology relation induced by pangenome graphs, supporting graph comparison across variation graph and whole genome alignment models. What is new is the explicit definition of diversity and homology on graph structure itself, shifting analysis from sequences toward graph-derived quantities. The other two items do not operate on pangenome graphs. SLAB is a sweep-line algorithm over the PBWT for finding haplotype block cores and width-maximal matches in UK Biobank haplotypes. A median-tree consensus study uses transfer and quartet dissimilarities in place of Robinson-Foulds for phylogenetic consensus.
